claims.sentence: The MHRA says large studies of millions of children have found no evidence that vaccines cause autism, and reaffirms the safety of childhood vaccination.
claims.evidence: MHRA statement summary: Dr Alison Cave (Chief Safety Officer) quoted: multiple large, well-conducted studies involving millions of children worldwide have consistently demonstrated no evidence that vaccines cause autism.

claims.sentence: The MHRA published its statement reaffirming the safety of childhood vaccination on 12 August 2026.
claims.evidence: Search text says the 'the' version is about 82 days old (roughly mid-August 2026) and 'the page itself doesn't show a date'; the other version is about 343 days old. Exact day 12 August not retrieved.

claims.sentence: Its Chief Safety Officer, Dr Alison Cave, says large, well-conducted studies of millions of children worldwide consistently show no evidence that vaccines cause autism.
claims.evidence: MHRA statement summary: Dr Alison Cave (Chief Safety Officer) quoted: multiple large, well-conducted studies involving millions of children worldwide have consistently demonstrated no evidence that vaccines cause autism. Caveat: retrieval did not show which of the two pages carries the quote; the older page is also described as carrying it.

claims.sentence: The statement cites a study of 2.56 million US children that found no link between MMR vaccination before age 2 and autism.
claims.evidence: Search 3: the more recent release ('reaffirms the safety of...') cites a US study of 2.56 million children, no association between MMR before age 2 and autism. Search 1 did not find the figure, but listed a 1.26 million meta-analysis in the notes; the 2.56m is attributed to the 'the' (2026) page only.

claims.sentence: The MHRA says it monitors vaccine safety continuously.
claims.evidence: Continuous surveillance wording was retrieved only for the 'Hepatitis B vaccines for babies' page notes, not for either childhood-vaccination page.

claims.sentence: The MHRA has published a statement reaffirming the safety of childhood vaccination.
claims.evidence: Page title 'MHRA reaffirms the safety of childhood vaccination'.

claims.sentence: Dr Alison Cave, the MHRA's Chief Safety Officer, says that multiple large, well-conducted studies involving millions of children worldwide consistently show no evidence that vaccines cause autism.
claims.evidence: MHRA statement summary: Dr Alison Cave (Chief Safety Officer) quoted: multiple large, well-conducted studies involving millions of children worldwide have consistently demonstrated no evidence that vaccines cause autism.

claims.sentence: The notes to the statement cite a study of 2.56 million children in the United States that found no association between MMR vaccination before age 2 and childhood autism.
claims.evidence: As c04 (notes to editors of the 2026 release).

claims.sentence: The statement also points to a recent large study that found no evidence of increased risk of neurodevelopmental disorders, including autism, from early childhood exposure to aluminium-containing vaccines.
claims.evidence: The aluminium-vaccine study wording was retrieved from the separate 'Vaccine safety' patient factsheet, not from either news page. Search 1 says the release itself only notes aluminium is a common adjuvant not used in MMR.

claims.sentence: The MHRA says it monitors vaccine safety continuously through the Yellow Card scheme, analysis of large healthcare datasets, review of international safety data and ongoing review by independent scientific experts.
claims.evidence: Yellow Card/datasets/international data wording retrieved only for the Hepatitis B page; 'independent scientific experts' not seen anywhere. Ledger itself notes this was unresolved.

claims.sentence: Dr Cave encouraged parents to follow NHS vaccination guidance and to speak to a healthcare professional if they have questions.
claims.evidence: Not present in any retrieved text. Also an instruction to individuals (flagged).

claims.sentence: The site's autism page explains the condition.
claims.evidence: Site-navigation gloss, not from the source or any retrieved text.

dateEvidence: Search results gave relative ages only: '...reaffirms-the-safety-of-...' ~82 days old (mid-Aug 2026, consistent with but not confirming 12 Aug); '...reaffirms-safety-of-...' ~343 days old (about Nov 2025). The page shows no date in the retrieved text. Which URL is 2026 is confirmed by relative age; exact day is not.
notes: Source URL in brief is the 'the' (2026) page: correct.
